claim: Canonical's Real-time Ubuntu documentation, 'Real-time Ubuntu releases' table (Ubuntu Server / Desktop): Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, RT kernel 6.8, variants 'generic, raspi'; Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (Resolute Raccoon), RT kernel 7.0, variants 'generic, raspi'; Ubuntu 26.10, RT kernel 7.3, variants 'generic, raspi'. So Canonical documents a Raspberry Pi real-time variant for 26.04, not only for 24.04. [status note: the table names no Pi model; which boards the 26.04 raspi RT kernel boots was not verified]

Canonical's 'How to enable Real-time Ubuntu', tab 'Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (Resolute Raccoon) or newer': 'Real-time Ubuntu can be installed from the main archive: sudo apt install ubuntu-realtime'; note: 'On Raspberry Pi, install linux-raspi-realtime instead'. The 24.04-or-earlier tab points to the Ubuntu Pro Client (pro enable). [status note: the 26.04 archive does not resolve from this session, so the presence of linux-raspi-realtime in resolute was not checked in the archive itself; Repology listed no 26.04 entry (C-FIX7-003, SECONDARY)]

Eclipse Mosquitto ChangeLog: release '1.6 - 20190417', section '# Broker features', first item 'Add support for MQTT v5'; release '2.0.22 - 2025-07-11' is in the same file. The mosquitto 2.0.22 that Repology lists for 26.04 (C-FIX7-004) is therefore an MQTT 5 broker

go-fdo-client (Apache-2.0) has a tagged release v1.0.0, published 2026-02-19. Its go.mod at v1.0.0 pins the go-fdo library to an untagged pseudo-version (v0.0.0-20260204145003-2d3d7c734680). The client's README documents a --tpm option (for example /dev/tpmrm0) for device credential secrets. Its only packaging is an RPM spec (build/package/rpm/go-fdo-client.spec) plus a Packit config that targets Fedora and CentOS; the repository has no Debian or Ubuntu packaging
go-fdo-server has a tagged release v1.0.2, published 2026-10-08; at that tag its only packaging is build/package/rpm/go-fdo-server.spec plus .packit.yaml (no Debian/Ubuntu packaging)

go-fdo README at its current main commit, line 11: 'This library has not yet completed interop testing with the FIDO Alliance, but will at the next opportunity.' The repository has no tags or releases (re-read 2026-11-11; pins C-REF4-DC-technical-004 to a SHA)

Landscape 26.10 release notes: 'Landscape Server 26.10 runs on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Resolute Raccoon, 24.04 LTS Noble Numbat, or 22.04 LTS Jammy Jellyfish'; the new compliance report 'returns a compliance and security report for up to 10,000 instances'

Landscape REST API, package change plans: 'The instance selection may target at most 100 instances. The package selection may target at most 500 packages.' Landscape's package management acts on deb packages and snaps (web-portal guide: up to 100 instances at once); the documentation describes no handling of RAUC or other A/B image bundles [status note: absence inferred from a grep of the whole docs tree for 'rauc' and 'A/B' at this commit]
Landscape docs: 'Landscape SaaS ... bundled with your Ubuntu Pro subscription' (what-is-landscape.md L48); tutorial: 'Ubuntu Pro is free for up to 5 machines' (tutorial.md L45)

RAUC documentation, 'Deployment via Deployment Server': 'RAUC focuses on update handling on the target side, it does not provide a deployment server out of the box'; it names Eclipse hawkBit, which 'provides some strategies for rollout management for larger-scale device farms', the C rauc-hawkbit-updater bridge (hawkBit DDI API to RAUC D-Bus API), a Python rauc-hawkbit client, Upparat (AWS IoT Jobs), qbee and an AWS IoT Greengrass component

Eclipse hawkBit 1.2.0 was released on 2026-11-11 (1.1.0 on 2026-07-03). The release notes list target group quotas, per-tenant DB connection throttling (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) and assignment-performance work, and move the baseline to Java 25 and Spring Boot 4.1.2. The RAUC fleet backend is actively maintained
